places.title: Duomo di Milano
places.architect: Veneranda Fabbrica del Duomo (Simone da Orsenigo and many others)
places.why: The largest church in Italy, built over almost six centuries in pink-veined white marble from Candoglia, with a forest of spires, pinnacles and thousands of statues. Its roof terraces lead between the flying buttresses up to the foot of the gilded Madonnina, with views over the city to the Alps.

photos.file: Milano, Duomo with Milan Cathedral and Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, 2016.jpg
photos.author: Steffen Schmitz

places.title: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
places.why: Two glass-vaulted arcades of iron and glass cross under an octagonal dome, joining Piazza del Duomo to Piazza della Scala. With its mosaic floors and four storeys of decorated fronts, it set the model for the covered shopping streets of the 19th century and remains the city's grand public room.

photos.file: Veduta della Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II da piazza del Duomo, Milano.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140

photos.file: Milano - Galleria Vittorio Emanuele - Vista dall alto dell Ottagono e lunette.jpg
photos.author: Angels1964

photos.file: Milano - Galleria Vittorio Emanuele - Vista interna della cupola al centro dell'Ottagono.jpg
photos.author: Angels1964

places.title: Santa Maria delle Grazie
places.why: A Dominican church whose Gothic brick nave by Guiniforte Solari ends in Bramante's Renaissance tribune, a great cube under a sixteen-sided drum. In the refectory of the convent is Leonardo's Last Supper; church and painting are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

photos.file: Santa Maria delle Grazie Milano (Cenacolo Vinciano) 01.jpg
photos.author: FrDr

photos.file: Santa Maria delle Grazie - Joy of Museums.jpg
photos.author: Joyofmuseums

places.title: Castello Sforzesco
places.architect: Galeazzo II Visconti; Francesco Sforza; Luca Beltrami (restoration)
places.why: The brick fortress and residence of the Visconti and Sforza dukes, with round corner towers and a sequence of vast courtyards behind the Filarete Tower, rebuilt by Luca Beltrami. It closes the axis that runs from the Duomo along Via Dante to Parco Sempione.

places.title: Parco Sempione
places.architect: Emilio Alemagna (park); Luigi Cagnola (Arco della Pace); Luigi Canonica (Arena Civica)
places.why: An English landscape park on the old parade ground behind the castle, with lawns, a pond and winding paths. At its far end the neoclassical Arco della Pace, begun for Napoleon, faces the castle down a straight perspective; around it stand the Arena Civica of 1807, the Triennale and the Torre Branca.

places.title: Teatro alla Scala and Piazza della Scala
places.why: Piermarini's opera house has a sober neoclassical front and a horseshoe hall of boxes and galleries in six tiers, in red and gold. Across the square stand Galeazzo Alessi's Palazzo Marino, the city hall, and the palaces of the Gallerie d'Italia, where the bank collections of 19th-century art are shown.

photos.file: Veduta del Palazzo della Banca Commerciale Italiana, piazza della Scala, Milano, tre quarti da sinistra.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140

places.title: Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio
places.architect: Founded by Saint Ambrose; Donato Bramante (Canonica portico)
places.why: Founded by Saint Ambrose in the 4th century and rebuilt in the 11th and 12th, it is the model of Lombard Romanesque: an arcaded brick atrium, two bell towers of different ages and a nave of ribbed vaults. Inside are the golden altar of the 9th century and early Christian mosaics.

places.title: Navigli and the Darsena
places.why: The last open stretches of the canals that once carried marble for the Duomo and goods to the city, meeting in the Darsena, the old harbour. Their towpaths are lined with low houses, courtyard tenements and the covered washhouse of the Vicolo dei Lavandai, and fill with people in the evening.

photos.file: Naviglio Grande near San Cristoforo sul Naviglio-Milan-Italy.jpg
photos.author: FlavMi

places.title: Brera
places.architect: Francesco Maria Richini; Giuseppe Piermarini (Palazzo di Brera)
places.why: A district of narrow cobbled streets and low ochre houses around the Palazzo di Brera, a Jesuit college by Francesco Maria Richini with a two-storey arcaded courtyard, home to the Pinacoteca, the Academy of Fine Arts and a small botanical garden. Next door, Palazzo Citterio reopened in 2024 as part of the Grande Brera museum.

photos.author: Foto eseguita da socio di ARASS-Brera in nome e per conto dell'Associazione.

photos.file: Veduta laterale del Palazzo di Brera, Milano.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140

places.title: Quadrilatero della moda
places.why: The grid of streets between Via Monte Napoleone, Via Manzoni, Via della Spiga and Corso Venezia, lined with neoclassical palaces whose ground floors hold the flagship shops of the fashion houses. Behind the gates are quiet courtyards and house museums such as the Bagatti Valsecchi and Palazzo Morando.

places.title: Cimitero Monumentale
places.why: A walled cemetery that is an open-air museum of Milanese sculpture and architecture from the 1860s to the 1930s: the striped marble Famedio in Lombard-Byzantine style, family chapels in every revival style and Art Nouveau, and modern memorials such as the BBPR monument to the deportees.

photos.file: Cimitero Monumentale di Milano nella sua vista esterna frontale.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140

places.title: Stazione di Milano Centrale
places.why: The largest railway station in Europe by volume: a monumental stone front in a mix of Liberty and Art Deco, with winged horses on the cornice, opens onto a sequence of vaulted halls and five iron and glass train sheds over the platforms.

places.title: Porta Nuova and Piazza Gae Aulenti
places.architect: Pelli Clarke Pelli (UniCredit Tower and square); Mario Cucinella Architects (Torre Unipol); Pelli Clarke & Partners (Gioia 22)
places.why: The business district built since 2009 on old railway land between Garibaldi station and Isola. Its centre is Piazza Gae Aulenti, a round raised square with fountains under the spire of the UniCredit Tower, the tallest building in Italy, joined by bridges and gardens to Bosco Verticale and the Biblioteca degli Alberi.

places.title: Bosco Verticale
places.architect: Boeri Studio (Stefano Boeri, Gianandrea Barreca, Giovanni La Varra)
places.why: Two residential towers whose staggered concrete balconies carry hundreds of trees and thousands of shrubs of some ninety species, set in deep planters. The facades change colour with the seasons, and the greenery is tended by climbers who abseil down the towers.

places.title: Stadio San Siro (Giuseppe Meazza)
places.architect: Ulisse Stacchini, Alberto Cugini (1926); Armando Ronca, Ferruccio Calzolari (1955); Giancarlo Ragazzi, Enrico Hoffer (1990)
places.why: The stadium of AC Milan and Inter, enlarged for the 1990 World Cup with eleven cylindrical towers of spiral ramps that carry a third ring of stands; four of them hold up the roof on red steel girders.

places.title: Piazza dei Mercanti
places.why: The medieval civic centre, a small enclosed square a few steps from the Duomo. The Palazzo della Ragione stands on an open arcade where the market was held; the Loggia degli Osii, striped in black and white marble, has the balcony from which decrees were proclaimed.

photos.file: Palazzo della Ragione (a destra nella foto), Milano.jpg
photos.author: Margherito1

places.title: Colonne and Basilica di San Lorenzo
places.why: Sixteen Roman columns, reused in late antiquity, stand in a row in front of one of the oldest churches of the West, a 4th-century central plan with four towers under a Renaissance dome. Behind it the Parco delle Basiliche runs as a long lawn to Sant'Eustorgio.

photos.file: Milano - Basilica san Lorenzo a porta Ticinese.jpg
photos.author: Blackcat
Original uploader was Bigorenzo at it.wikipedia

places.title: Fondazione Prada
places.why: A gin distillery of 1910 turned into an arts centre: OMA kept the industrial sheds and added an exhibition hall, a cinema and a white concrete tower of galleries. The old Haunted House is clad in gold leaf, and the café inside was designed by the film director Wes Anderson.

photos.file: P za Olivetti e F Prada da v Orobia LU02708.jpg
photos.author: Lalupa

photos.file: P za Olivetti, la fontana e edificio Fastweb LU02696.jpg
photos.author: Lalupa

places.title: Grattacielo Pirelli
places.architect: Gio Ponti, Antonio Fornaroli, Alberto Rosselli, Giuseppe Valtolina, Egidio Dell'Orto; Pier Luigi Nervi, Arturo Danusso (structure)
places.why: Gio Ponti's 127-metre tower has a slim lozenge plan with tapered ends, so from the side it reads as a thin blade. Instead of a steel frame, Pier Luigi Nervi carried it on tapering concrete piers and triangular cores at the ends; it is now the seat of the Lombardy regional council.

places.title: Fondazione Feltrinelli and Microsoft House
places.why: Two long, narrow buildings on the line of the old Spanish walls, their steep gables and pitched roofs taken from Lombard farm buildings and stretched into a sloping grid of concrete and glass. One holds the library of the Feltrinelli Foundation, the other the Italian offices of Microsoft.

places.title: Università Bocconi: Roentgen building and SANAA campus
places.why: Grafton Architects hung the offices and lecture halls of the Roentgen building from a deep stone and concrete structure over a public foyer open to the street. Nearby, SANAA's campus of 2019 wraps classrooms, student housing and a public sports centre with an Olympic pool in curved, transparent volumes veiled in aluminium mesh, around a park.

places.title: CityLife
places.architect: Arata Isozaki (Allianz Tower); Zaha Hadid Architects (Generali Tower, Residenze Hadid); Studio Libeskind (PwC Tower, Residenze Libeskind); Gustafson Porter + Bowman, One Works (park)
places.why: The old trade fair grounds rebuilt around three towers nicknamed the straight, the twisted and the curved: Isozaki's glass slab braced by golden buttresses, Zaha Hadid's tower turning on its axis and Daniel Libeskind's curved tower. Around them stand Hadid's housing with flowing white balconies, Libeskind's angular blocks, a shopping street and a large park.

photos.file: Tre Torri, Milan, Italy Apr 14, 2023 07-56-42 PM.jpeg
photos.author: KaiKemmann

photos.file: Residenze Hadid, CityLife district, Milan, Italy 03 00 33 307000.jpeg
photos.author: KaiKemmann

photos.file: Residenze Hadid, CityLife district, Milan, Italy.jpeg
photos.author: KaiKemmann
Franco Dal Molin from Milano, Italia

places.title: MUDEC – Museo delle Culture
places.why: David Chipperfield turned the former Ansaldo engineering works into a museum of world cultures: boxy galleries clad in zinc around a curving hall of translucent glass that serves as a covered square and glows at night like a lantern.

photos.file: Mudec - Museo delle culture, primo piano.jpg
photos.author: FrussiWMI

photos.file: Milano - MUDEC - Museo delle Culture - Particolare dell'Agorà.jpg
photos.author: Silvana Gallio

photos.file: Mudec, Agorà, Ingresso alla Collezione Permanente.jpg
photos.author: Hime sara

places.title: Museo del Novecento (Arengario)
places.architect: Piero Portaluppi, Giovanni Muzio, Pier Giulio Magistretti, Enrico Agostino Griffini (Arengario); Italo Rota, Fabio Fornasari (museum)
places.why: Twin arcaded pavilions of white stone built on Piazza del Duomo in the 1930s now hold the city's collection of 20th-century art. A spiral ramp climbs through the building to a glass room facing the cathedral spires, lit by Lucio Fontana's neon arabesque.

places.title: Biblioteca e Pinacoteca Ambrosiana
places.architect: Francesco Maria Richini, Fabio Mangone; Giacomo Moraglia (19th-century front)
places.why: One of the first public libraries in Europe, founded by Cardinal Federico Borromeo in 1609. The Sala Federiciana, with two tiers of wooden shelves under a barrel vault, and the picture gallery around the courtyards keep Leonardo's Codex Atlanticus, his Musician and Caravaggio's Basket of Fruit.

photos.file: Veduta della Biblioteca Ambrosiana, Milano, di tre quarti.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140

places.title: San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore
places.architect: Gian Giacomo Dolcebuono, Giovanni Antonio Amadeo
places.why: A plain Renaissance church divided by a wall into a hall for the public and a choir for the nuns of the Monastero Maggiore. Every surface of both halls is covered in frescoes by Bernardino Luini and his school.

photos.file: Milano - Chiesa di San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore - 2023-09-23 21-11-18 001.jpg
photos.author: LaHantucci

photos.file: Milano - Chiesa di San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore - 2023-09-24 23-57-52 003.jpg
photos.author: 01albertop

photos.file: Milano - Chiesa di San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore - 2023-09-24 23-57-52 006.jpg
photos.author: 01albertop

places.title: Villa Necchi Campiglio
places.why: A villa of the 1930s built by Piero Portaluppi for an industrial family, in a walled garden with the first private swimming pool in Milan. Its rooms keep the rationalist geometry, rare woods, marbles and machine-age fittings of the period, softened by later classical touches from Tommaso Buzzi.

places.title: Triennale Milano (Palazzo dell'Arte)
places.why: Giovanni Muzio's exhibition palace on the edge of Parco Sempione, a long building of brick and clinker with a monumental arched entrance and a grand staircase, built for the design and architecture shows of the Triennale. It houses the Italian Design Museum.

photos.file: " 12 - ITALY - Triennale Design Museum - Milan Design Week 2012 (fuorisalone) Triennale di Milano 2.JPG
photos.author: Pava

places.title: Torre Branca
places.architect: Gio Ponti; Cesare Chiodi, Ettore Ferrari (engineers)
places.why: A steel lattice tower 108 metres high, put up by Gio Ponti in 68 days for the Triennale of 1933 and kept just below the Madonnina of the Duomo. A lift climbs to a viewing cabin above the trees of Parco Sempione.

places.title: Casa Galimberti and Casa Guazzoni
places.why: Two Liberty apartment houses by Giovanni Battista Bossi a few steps apart. Casa Galimberti is covered in ceramic tiles painted with figures and flowers and has wrought-iron balconies; Casa Guazzoni trades the tiles for stucco garlands, cherubs and curling iron railings.

places.title: Palazzo Castiglioni
places.why: The manifesto of Milanese Art Nouveau on Corso Venezia: a rusticated stone front that grows lighter as it rises, with sculpted foliage, putti and wrought iron. The two nude figures that once flanked the door caused a scandal and were moved to another building.

places.title: Casa Museo Boschi Di Stefano
places.why: An apartment house by Piero Portaluppi with an Art Deco front, where a collector couple left their home to the city with its furniture and some 300 Italian paintings of the 20th century hung on every wall.

photos.file: Casa Boschi Di Stefano, le scale 1.jpg
photos.author: Angelo0053

places.title: PAC – Padiglione d'Arte Contemporanea
places.why: Ignazio Gardella's exhibition pavilion beside the Villa Reale garden, a low building of brick screens and glass with galleries on split levels that open onto the trees. Destroyed by a Mafia car bomb in 1993, it was rebuilt to his design.

photos.file: PAC - Padiglione d'Arte Contemporanea di Milano.jpg
photos.author: Pava

places.title: Museo della Scienza e della Tecnologia
places.why: The national science museum fills a 16th-century Olivetan monastery with two cloisters, where models of Leonardo's machines stand along the old galleries. Pavilions in the grounds hold steam locomotives, a submarine and a sailing ship.

photos.file: Chiostri del Museo Nazionale Scienza e Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci.jpg
photos.author: Paolo Soave

photos.file: Milano - Museo nazionale della scienza e della tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci - 2025-09-12 20-33-35 002.jpg
photos.author: Antonina Dattola

photos.file: Milano - Museo nazionale della scienza e della tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci.jpg
photos.author: 01albertop

places.title: Basilica di Sant'Eustorgio and the Portinari Chapel
places.why: A Romanesque basilica on the old road to Pavia that once held relics of the Magi. Behind the apse, the Portinari Chapel is one of the first Renaissance works in Milan: a cube under a ribbed dome, frescoed by Vincenzo Foppa.

photos.file: Portinari Chapel, 1460-68; Basilica of Sant'Eustorgio, Milan.jpg
photos.author: Prof. Mortel

places.title: Palazzo Reale
places.why: The old seat of the city's rulers beside the Duomo, given a sober neoclassical front by Giuseppe Piermarini for the Austrian archduke. The Sala delle Cariatidi, its great ballroom, has been kept as the bombs of 1943 left it.

photos.file: Veduta di tre quarti del Palazzo Reale di Milano.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140

places.title: Villa Reale (Villa Belgiojoso Bonaparte)
places.why: A neoclassical villa with a columned garden front, built for Count Belgiojoso and later home to Napoleon and Eugène de Beauharnais; it houses the Modern Art Gallery. Behind it lies one of the first English landscape gardens in Italy, with a pond, a small temple and old trees.

photos.file: Milano, villa reale, prospetto sul parco.jpg
photos.author: Sailko

places.title: Ca' Granda (Ospedale Maggiore)
places.architect: Filarete; Guiniforte Solari; Francesco Maria Richini; Liliana Grassi and others (post-war reconstruction)
places.why: The city hospital founded by Francesco Sforza, laid out by Filarete as cross-shaped wards around courtyards behind a long brick front with terracotta ornament. Bombed in 1943, it was rebuilt as the main seat of the State University; its great courtyard by Richini is open to all.

places.title: Piazza degli Affari and Palazzo Mezzanotte
places.why: The square of the stock exchange, framed by Paolo Mezzanotte's travertine palace with giant columns and allegorical reliefs. In front of it stands Maurizio Cattelan's marble hand with only its middle finger raised.

places.title: Piazzale Cadorna and Cadorna station
places.architect: Gae Aulenti (square and station front); Claes Oldenburg, Coosje van Bruggen (Ago, filo e nodo)
places.why: Gae Aulenti remade the square and the front of the Ferrovie Nord station for the Jubilee of 2000, with a canopy of coloured steel tubes over the entrance. In the middle stands Oldenburg and van Bruggen's giant needle and thread in the colours of the metro lines, its knot rising from a pool.

photos.file: Milano - Piazzale Cadorna e Stazione Ferrovie Nord - panoramio.jpg
photos.author: MarkusMark

photos.file: Entrée sur le côté du parvis de la gare de Milano Cadorna.jpg
photos.author: Remontees

places.title: Piccolo Teatro Strehler
places.why: The home of the Piccolo Teatro, the first public theatre in Italy: Marco Zanuso's red-brick building holds a fan-shaped hall of almost a thousand seats.

places.title: Palazzo Lombardia
places.architect: Pei Cobb Freed & Partners (Henry N. Cobb); Caputo Partnership; Sistema Duemila
places.why: The seat of the regional government: curving office wings that interlace around a covered public square, with a 161-metre glass tower at the centre, briefly the tallest building in Italy. A viewing terrace near the top looks over the new skyline.

places.title: Casa della Memoria
places.why: A plain block for the archives of the Resistance and the deportations, whose brick walls form a giant mosaic of portraits and scenes from the city's 20th-century history. It stands between the low streets of Isola and the towers of Porta Nuova.

photos.file: Casa della Memoria esterno a colori.jpg
photos.author: Ettorre (gregorio)

places.title: Fondazione Luigi Rovati
places.why: A 19th-century palazzo on Corso Venezia converted into a museum of Etruscan and contemporary art. Below it, Mario Cucinella carved a domed underground gallery lined in stone, inspired by Etruscan tombs.

photos.file: Milano - Fondazione Luigi Rovati - Museo d'arte - 2024-09-01 20-46-52 001.jpg
photos.author: Barbaragerosa

photos.file: Milano - Fondazione Luigi Rovati - Museo d'arte - 2024-09-01 20-55-58 001.jpg
photos.author: Barbaragerosa

photos.file: Milano - Fondazione Luigi Rovati - Museo d'arte - 2024-09-01 20-49-34 001.jpg
photos.author: Barbaragerosa

places.title: Fiera Milano Rho
places.why: The trade fair grounds that replaced the old fair in the city, laid along a central walkway 1.3 kilometres long under a roof of glass and steel that swells into funnels, craters and waves. The roof, called the Vela, joins the pavilions on both sides.

places.title: Palazzo Mondadori
places.architect: Oscar Niemeyer; Pietro Porcinai (garden and lake)
places.why: Oscar Niemeyer's headquarters for the publisher: a glass office block hung from a row of concrete arches of different widths, mirrored in an artificial lake laid out with the gardens by Pietro Porcinai.
places.note: Private offices: the building is seen from outside the grounds.

photos.file: Mondadori headquarters by Oscar Niemeyer, Segrate (Milano) 07.jpg
photos.author: Carlo Dell'Orto

photos.author: Carlo Dell'Orto

photos.author: Carlo Dell'Orto

photos.file: Mondadori headquarters by Oscar Niemeyer, Segrate (Milano) 05.jpg
photos.author: Carlo Dell'Orto

places.title: Portello: Piazza Gino Valle and Parco del Portello
places.architect: Valle Architetti Associati (square); Charles Jencks with LAND (park); Cino Zucchi Architetti (housing)
places.why: The former Alfa Romeo works rebuilt as a new district. Gino Valle's square, one of the largest in the city, opens between office buildings and is linked by a footbridge to Charles Jencks's park, where three grassy spiral mounds stand for prehistory, history and the future; around them rise Cino Zucchi's housing blocks.

places.title: RCS offices (Corriere della Sera)
places.architect: Boeri Studio (Stefano Boeri, Gianandrea Barreca, Giovanni La Varra)
places.why: The offices of the publisher of the Corriere della Sera on the eastern edge of the city: a C-shaped block of five storeys around a courtyard open to Via Rizzoli, with a slender tower 80 metres high.

places.title: Cascina Merlata
places.architect: Mario Cucinella Architects; Cino Zucchi Architetti; C+S Architects and others
places.why: A new residential quarter beside the Expo 2015 site, built around a 30-hectare park with a canal recalling the old springs. Its towers, first used as the Expo village and then as social housing, include Mario Cucinella's, Cino Zucchi's tapering towers with patterned facades and C+S Architects' towers with public space at their foot.

photos.file: Parcheggio selvaggio in via Pasolini a Milano nel quartiere Cascina Merlata nei pressi del centro commerciale Merlata Bloom.jpg
photos.author: Marcuscalabresus

places.title: Apple Piazza Liberty
places.why: A stepped amphitheatre of grey Lombard stone descends from the square to the shop below, behind a glass wall over which a fountain falls. The steps stay open to the city as a place to sit and meet.

photos.file: Piazza del liberty Milano da dietro 2018.jpg
photos.author: Marcuscalabresus

places.title: Monte Rosa 91 (former Il Sole 24 Ore headquarters)
places.why: Renzo Piano turned a three-winged industrial building into the newspaper's headquarters, wrapping it in a glass skin and filling the courtyard with a planted hill. The renewal of 2023 reworked the garden as the Parco della Luce, with works by three artists.

places.title: Residenze Carlo Erba
places.architect: Eisenman Architects with Degli Esposti Architetti and Guido Zuliani
places.why: Peter Eisenman's housing block rethinks the city's apartment house: a travertine base, a recessed floor and above it a grid that is filled in, left as an open frame or broken, as the building winds through its triangular lot around a garden.

places.title: IULM University building (IULM 6)
places.why: Three buildings for the university of communication: a tower around a spiral staircase that holds the archives and the digital library, its orange facades a favourite backdrop for photographers.

photos.file: Libera Università di Lingue e Comunicazone IULM, Milano.jpg
photos.author: DaveM93

places.title: Basilica di San Simpliciano
places.why: One of the basilicas founded by Saint Ambrose, its late Roman brick walls still standing to their full height behind a Romanesque front. In the apse, Bergognone's fresco of the Coronation of the Virgin floats over the altar.

places.title: Basilica di San Nazaro in Brolo
places.why: Another basilica of Saint Ambrose, a cross-shaped church on the old road to Rome, fronted by the Trivulzio Chapel, Bramantino's octagonal mausoleum with the family tombs in high niches. The square in front of it was redesigned in the 1990s.

photos.file: La Basilica di San Nazaro in Brolo, Milano, veduta della Cappella Trivulzio.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140

places.title: San Bernardino alle Ossa
places.why: A baroque church whose side chapel, the ossuary, has its walls lined with skulls and bones from the old hospital cemetery, set in patterns around the doors and pilasters, under a vault frescoed by Sebastiano Ricci.

photos.file: Altar of the Ossuary of San Bernardino alle Ossa, Milan.jpg
photos.author: Julian Lupyan

photos.file: Corner and Pendentive of the Ossuary of San Bernardino alle Ossa, Milan.jpg
photos.author: Julian Lupyan

places.title: Quadrilatero del silenzio
places.architect: Aldo Andreani (Casa Sola-Busca); Giulio Ulisse Arata (Casa Berri-Meregalli)
places.why: The quiet streets between Corso Venezia and Via Mozart, lined with villas and apartment houses of the early 20th century. Casa Berri-Meregalli mixes Romanesque, Gothic and Liberty with mosaics and wrought iron; Casa Sola-Busca has an intercom shaped like a bronze ear; pink flamingos live in the garden of Villa Invernizzi.

places.title: Pirelli HangarBicocca
places.why: A former factory of the Breda works, where locomotives and electrical machinery were built, turned into one of the largest exhibition spaces in Europe. Its cathedral-like main hall permanently houses Anselm Kiefer's Seven Heavenly Palaces, towers of stacked concrete.

photos.file: HangarBicocca, vue du haut du Hangar.jpg
photos.author: The42grabber

places.title: Abbazia di Chiaravalle
places.why: A Cistercian abbey founded by Bernard of Clairvaux in the farmland south of the city. Its brick church is crowned by a tall octagonal tower of stacked arcades, nicknamed the Ciribiciaccola, and monks still live around the cloister.

photos.author: The original uploader was Yoruno at Italian Wikipedia .

photos.file: Milano - chiesa dell'abbazia di Chiaravalle - Coro ligneo del presbiterio.jpg
photos.author: Angels1964

places.title: Piscina Romano
places.why: An open-air public pool of 1929, 100 metres long and 40 wide, built in six months by Luigi Lorenzo Secchi for 1,500 swimmers, between symmetrical changing pavilions with classical pediments.

photos.file: Piscina Guido Romano - View Via Ampere - Summer 2017.jpg
photos.author: Faffoman

places.title: Ca' Brutta
places.why: Giovanni Muzio's first work, an apartment block whose arches, niches, cornices and bands of coloured plaster are laid flat on the facade in a free pattern. The Milanese called it the ugly house; it became the manifesto of the Novecento movement.

photos.file: Paolo Monti – Milano. Ca' Brutta, 1982 circa – BEIC IE9091089.jpg
photos.author: Paolo Monti

places.title: Casa e Torre Rasini
places.why: Facing the toll gates of Porta Venezia and the public gardens, one project in two parts marks the old edge of the city: a block of six floors clad in white marble and a twelve-storey tower in banded brick, with a bay window and terraces stepping down to the garden.

photos.file: Paolo Monti – Milano. Palazzo e Torre Rasini, 1982 circa – BEIC IE9092271.jpg
photos.author: Paolo Monti

places.title: Casa Lavezzari
places.why: One of the apartment houses that Lingeri and Terragni built in Milan in the 1930s, a landmark of rationalism on a wedge-shaped lot with a narrow front on Piazza Morbegno.

places.title: Towers of Piazza della Repubblica
places.architect: Luigi Mattioni and others (Torre Breda); Giovanni Muzio (Torre Turati)
places.why: Milan's first skyscrapers rose in the 1950s around Piazza della Repubblica on the road from the old centre to the new station: the 117-metre Torre Breda of offices and flats, and Giovanni Muzio's stone-clad Torre Turati.

photos.file: Piazza della Repubblica - ingresso linea 3 metropolitana - Milano (cropped).JPG
photos.author: Stefano Stabile

places.title: Torre Velasca
places.architect: BBPR (Gian Luigi Banfi, Lodovico Barbiano di Belgiojoso, Enrico Peressutti, Ernesto Nathan Rogers)
places.why: A 106-metre tower whose top floors of flats jut out over the offices below on slanting concrete brackets, like the keep of a medieval castle. Its restoration, finished in 2025, renewed the facades and opened a public square at its foot.

photos.file: Milano - Torre Velasca vista da Via Francesco Sforza - panoramio.jpg
photos.author: MarkusMark

places.title: Monte Amiata (Gallaratese)
places.why: Carlo Aymonino's red housing blocks gather around open-air theatres and raised streets, joined to Aldo Rossi's white slab, a gallery of thin square piers 182 metres long. The two architects made it a manifesto of the city as an assembly of streets, squares and porticoes.

places.title: Politecnico di Milano: Faculty of Architecture
places.architect: Giordano Forti, Gio Ponti, Piero Portaluppi (main building); Vittoriano Viganò, Fabrizio de Miranda (extension)
places.why: Beside the school's building by Ponti, Portaluppi and Forti, Vittoriano Viganò's extension is drawn by its structure: full-height black steel piers, tie rods and hanging white concrete stairs in front of a glazed facade, over a sunken courtyard where the students meet.

places.title: Monumento a Sandro Pertini
places.why: Aldo Rossi's monument to the President of the Republic is a small Lombard square: a flight of steps leads to a cube of grey-pink Candoglia marble, the stone of the Duomo, eight metres a side, with water running down a channel in its back wall.

places.title: Istituto Marchiondi Spagliardi
places.why: Vittoriano Viganò's boarding school for boys with social problems, a landmark of Italian brutalism: raw concrete frames, open galleries and separate blocks for dormitories, classrooms and workshops on a field at the edge of the city.
places.note: Abandoned and fenced: it can be seen only from the street.

photos.file: Paolo Monti – Milano. Istituto minorile Marchiondi Spagliardi, 1957 circa – BEIC IE9090762.jpg
photos.author: Paolo Monti

photos.file: Paolo Monti – Milano. Istituto minorile Marchiondi Spagliardi, 1957 circa – BEIC IE9090555.jpg
photos.author: Paolo Monti

places.title: Chiesa di San Giovanni Bono
places.why: The church at the centre of a public housing quarter by the same architect: walls of exposed concrete pierced by many small coloured windows, under a sail-like roof that rises from the altar to a sharp peak over the entrance.

photos.file: Milano - Chiesa di San Giovanni Bono - 2023-09-29 00-09-47 001.jpg
photos.author: Carlo318

photos.file: Milano chiesa San Giovanni Bono fianco est.JPG
photos.author: Arbalete

photos.file: Milano chiesa San Giovanni Bono altare.JPG
photos.author: Arbalete

places.title: Casa a tre cilindri
places.why: A block of flats built for a cooperative of civil servants as three cylindrical towers set in a garden, to give each flat light and independence; its unusual image made it one of the best-known works of its architects.

photos.file: Milano - casa a tre cilindri - vista.JPG
photos.author: Arbalete

places.title: Igloo houses of the Maggiolina
places.why: Small domed houses built in Via Lepanto after the war as quick homes for families who had lost theirs in the bombing. Only a couple keep their original form, among the villas of the garden district of the Villaggio dei Giornalisti.

places.title: Giardini Indro Montanelli
places.architect: Giuseppe Piermarini; Giuseppe Balzaretto, Emilio Alemagna (enlargements)
places.why: The first public garden of the city, laid out by Piermarini and later reshaped as an English landscape park with ponds, small bridges and old trees. It holds the Natural History Museum and Piero Portaluppi's Hoepli Planetarium.

photos.file: Veduta del Museo civico di storia naturale di Milano.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140

places.title: Giardini della Guastalla
places.why: The garden of a 16th-century college for girls of noble families, the oldest in the city: a baroque fishpond with balustrades, a small temple and tall trees in a quiet corner near the State University.

photos.file: Tempietto del Cagnola Giardini della Guastalla Milano.jpg
photos.author: Paolobon140
Original uploader was Yoruno at it.wikipedia

places.title: Parco Nord Milano
places.why: A large park of woods, meadows and ponds planted since the 1970s on farmland and the edge of the old Breda works north of the city, crossed by long cycle and walking paths.

places.title: Monte Stella and QT8
places.why: A wooded hill 45 metres high raised from the rubble of the wartime bombing as the green heart of QT8, an experimental quarter planned by Piero Bottoni for the Triennale of 1947. Its paths look over the city's towers and, on clear days, to the Alps.

places.title: Biblioteca degli Alberi (BAM)
places.architect: Inside Outside (Petra Blaisse) with Franco Giorgetta; Piet Oudolf (planting)
places.why: A public park between the towers of Porta Nuova, drawn as a web of straight paths crossing irregular fields of grass and flowers, with round groves each of one tree species, like a botanical library. Piet Oudolf planted its perennial borders.

places.title: Boscoincittà
places.architect: Italia Nostra (Centro per la Forestazione Urbana)
places.why: The first urban forest in Italy, planted by Italia Nostra with schools and volunteers since 1974 on farmland at the western edge of the city: woods, clearings, streams, a small lake, allotments and a 15th-century farmhouse.

places.title: Parco delle Cave
places.why: Four lakes in old gravel pits, with woods, streams, allotments and water meadows around the Cascina Linterno, form one of the largest parks of the city, joined to the Boscoincittà.

photos.file: Lago artificiale al tramonto, Parco delle Cave, Milano.jpg
photos.author: Mi ma1992

places.title: Parco Trotter
places.why: The track of an old trotting racecourse, abandoned in 1924, became the main avenue of an open-air school for children at risk of tuberculosis; its pavilions still stand among the trees around the oval.

places.title: Parco Forlanini
places.why: A large park opened in 1970 that keeps the pattern of the Lombard countryside: tree-lined paths, the Lambro river, a pond, an old mill and farmhouses, near Linate airport.

places.title: Parco Lambro
places.why: One of the largest parks of the city, designed in the 1930s by Enrico Casiraghi as a summary of the Lombard landscape, with hills, small lakes, oak woods and meadows along the river Lambro.

places.title: Idroscalo
places.why: A basin dug at the end of the 1920s as an airport for seaplanes, now known as the sea of Milan: a rowing course and beaches ringed by a park.

places.title: Naviglio della Martesana
places.why: The canal dug in the 15th century to bring the water of the Adda to the city, followed by a cycle and walking path that comes out at Cassina de' Pomm and passes the villas and gardens of Gorla and Crescenzago on its way out of town.
